items.text: after dictating or another app's sound, the Sound button checks that the sound really came back before saying so. If it is still silent, the chip stays and Reset becomes the white button. On a phone it also claims the sound back from the system first
on an iPad, the bug button sits in the top right corner, and the report opens there too
the path marks under the bar are small dots off each button's lower right: a filled dot with the path's number while it's open, a ring with a tiny tick once it's walked
when the sound comes back, the Sound / Reset chip says "Sound back" itself and then goes

coming back to Current while the sound kept playing in the background no longer kills it. The sound is checked first and only rescued if it really stopped, and only a tap (not a drag on the stage) restarts it. When the sound dips (dictating in another app) and comes back by itself, the Sound / Reset chip now goes away on its own

Clean output (Pro, open in beta). In Tools › session, output shows the stage alone in its own window for a projector or second screen, while this laptop keeps the controls. Chrome and Edge can move it onto the other screen; click it once to fill that screen. On a phone or tablet the cable mirrors the screen, so there it hides the controls instead
on a phone, the bug button is part of the report sheet's frame, so it always sits exactly on the sheet's close
the open padlock stands on its own (the outline around it is gone) and its shackle lifts a little every few seconds, so you can see it's open
on a phone, the bug button sits exactly where the report sheet's close button appears, so one spot opens and closes it
the Session sheet hands you the Link helper: the Link bridge downloads from there, with Carabiner's own download and the how-to beside it
on a phone, the bug report button sits in the top right corner once the namemark has stepped away, not beside the duck-rabbit

Session. Laptops in one room play in time: one starts a session and conducts, the others join with its four-letter code. The conductor's switch says what they follow: Free (each its own), Tempo (its beat), or Scenes (its beat and its scenes). Anyone can step out and back in. In Tools › session
Ableton Link for the conductor, through a small helper on that laptop (Carabiner and the Link bridge), so Current plays on the musicians' own Link tempo

Pro features being tested are open to everyone for now and wear an open padlock: Session, Blend, Water material, more saved beats, beat export. The version line on the cover says so; tap it for the list (also in Settings › Version)
the button at the end of the word field plays the word sequence, and stops it while it plays. Typing a change turns it back into the check that traces your word
